finding: Task POST and PATCH scoped task rows to the current user but accepted any projectId, so a user could create or attach a task to another user's project. Both routes now verify the destination project with the authenticated user before create/updateMany and return 404 without writing when it is not owned; PATCH checks supplied empty strings as well as nonempty ids.
tests: 7 tests passed across PATCH and POST project boundaries, including foreign/empty/owned/omitted/missing-task/unauthenticated cases. Earlier failed harness attempts remain recorded in checks/785c7da790a8.
limitations: Uses explicit Prisma/auth doubles rather than a live database.
Authentication wrapper and middleware are stubbed.
Ownership lookup and task update/create are separate operations, so concurrency behavior is not covered.

sourceMap.auth: withUser supplies the authenticated user id
sourceMap.validation: taskSchema parses POST fields; patchSchema parses PATCH fields, while tests use a parse-through double
sourceMap.authorization: Both routes use prisma.project.findFirst with destination project id and userId before task create/updateMany
sourceMap.persistence: POST creates with authenticated userId; PATCH updateMany remains user-scoped, followed by findUnique for the response
